title: Adaptive Phase Fragmentation with Kernel‑Hinting for Latency‑Sensitive Tenants
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: High-percentile latency for some small/interactive tenant requests spikes when the scheduler coalesces long prefill phases with decode-heavy phases on the same kernel path. Existing phase-splitting heuristics are throughput-optimized and insufficiently aware of kernel selection and attention-operator costs, which leads to head-of-line blocking for latency‑sensitive tenants.

Goal: Implement an adaptive phase fragmentation policy that propagates kernel hints from the profiling/kernels subsystem to the prefill/decode scheduler. The scheduler will use kernel cost estimates and attention‑operator specialization information to decide: (1) whether to split a request into micro-phases, (2) which micro-phases to coalesce, and (3) how to assign tenant-level hedging/fallback priorities to preserve latency SLOs while retaining reasonable throughput.

Non-goals: This ticket does not change kernel implementations themselves or modify quantization profiles. It focuses on scheduling decisions and hint propagation interfaces between scheduler and kernel cost estimator.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler implements kernel-hint-aware fragmentation that can be toggled per-tenant and per-route
End-to-end e2e benchmark: 95th percentile latency reduced by >=20% for latency-sensitive tenant workload (same config) without >10% regression on overall throughput
Canary rollout plan exists and is automated via console rollout config
Unit and integration tests for kernel hint propagation and fragmentation decisions with deterministic simulation
Observability: dashboards showing per-tenant phase-split rate, kernel-choice distribution, and latency/throughput trade-offs
plan: Design: define kernel-hint schema (cost-score, preferred-kernel-tag, attention-specialization-tag) with runtime team and ensure compact serializable form
Prototype: implement kernel-cost lookup in scheduler that consumes hints emitted by compilation/kernels service
Heuristic: develop fragmentation policy that creates micro-phases when predicted scheduling delay > latency_headroom for tenant, accounting for attention operator cost multiplier
Fairness: incorporate a token‑budget backoff so the fragmentation policy does not starve batch throughput — add soft quotas per-tenant per-window
Testing: extend existing simulator to model kernel switching overhead and KV cache warming; run synthetic mixes (interactive short, long-batch, bursty)
Benchmark: run end-to-end benchmarks on dedicated testpool with representative models (Llama-variant and transformer with sparse attention) and measure p50/p95/p99 and throughput
Rollout: staged canary 1% -> 10% -> 50% with automatic rollback on latency regressions, expose per-tenant toggle in Console
